title: Embedded, numeric, structural & testing idioms
literature: Preschern 'Fluent C'; Pont Patterns for Time-Triggered Embedded Systems; embedded C idioms; fixed-point/numeric; testing patterns (xUnit Patterns, Meszaros).

members.name: A/B Firmware Image Update
members.what: Keep two firmware image slots; write the new image into the inactive slot, verify it, then atomically switch the boot selection, keeping the old image as instant fallback.

members.name: Arbitrary-Precision Arithmetic
members.what: Represent and compute on integers (or rationals/decimals) whose size is limited only by memory, using multi-limb representations and carry-propagating algorithms instead of fixed-width machine words.

members.name: Bootloader Jump / Handoff
members.what: A small boot program validates the application image, then hands off execution by loading the application's stack pointer and reset vector (relocating the vector table) and jumping to it with hardware in a known state.

members.name: Checked Arithmetic
members.what: Integer arithmetic operations that report overflow explicitly (a boolean flag or Option/panic) instead of silently wrapping or invoking undefined behavior.

members.name: Composed Method
aka: compose methods out of intention-revealing calls
members.what: Structure a method as a short sequence of calls to other intention-named methods, all at a single level of abstraction.

members.name: Deferred Interrupt Processing
members.what: Split interrupt handling into a minimal ISR that acknowledges the hardware and queues work, plus deferred task-level code that completes the processing later.

members.name: Device Driver
members.what: A module encapsulating all interaction with one device class behind a uniform operations interface (open/read/write/ioctl or vendor API).

members.name: Direct Memory Access (DMA) Transfer
members.what: Configuring a DMA controller to move data between peripherals and memory without CPU involvement, with completion signaled by interrupt; often paired with double buffering so one buffer fills while the other is processed.

members.name: Epsilon/ULP Floating-Point Comparison
members.what: Comparing floating-point values for near-equality using an absolute/relative epsilon tolerance or a bounded distance in units-in-the-last-place (ULPs) instead of exact ==.

members.name: Escaping #ifdef Hell
members.what: Named patterns (avoid variants, isolated primitives, abstraction layer) that confine platform #ifdef variation to dedicated files behind common interfaces.

members.name: Feature Flag
members.what: A conditional branch point (toggle point) whose path is selected at runtime by a toggle router reading external toggle configuration, so a feature can be enabled or disabled without redeploying code.

members.name: Fixed-Point Arithmetic
members.what: Represent fractional values as scaled integers with an implicit binary point (Qm.n), doing real-number math with integer instructions.

members.name: Four-Phase Test
members.what: Structure every test as four ordered phases — fixture setup, exercise the system under test, result verification, fixture teardown — one behavior per test.

members.name: Generation Gap
members.what: Keep machine-generated code in a core base class that is never edited, and put all hand-written modifications in a subclass that survives regeneration unchanged.

members.name: Golden Master Testing
members.what: Captures the complete observed output of the system under test as a stored reference artifact (the golden master) and asserts that future runs reproduce it exactly, with an explicit approve-the-diff step when change is intended.

members.name: Hardware Adapter
members.what: An adapter layer that converts the interface a hardware device (or its proxy) actually offers into the interface the application expects.

members.name: Hardware Proxy
members.what: A class/module that encapsulates all access to a hardware device behind a device-neutral interface, hiding register layout, encoding, and access mechanics.

members.name: Hot Code Reload
members.what: Replaces a module's code in a running program, keeping old and new versions briefly coexistent and migrating state and in-flight control to the new version without a restart.

members.name: Humble Object
members.what: Strip hard-to-test code (GUI bindings, thread glue, framework touchpoints) down to a trivial 'humble' shell that immediately delegates all logic to a testable collaborator.

members.name: Include Guard
members.what: Preprocessor conditionals (or #pragma once) that make a header idempotent under multiple inclusion.

members.name: Interrupt Service Routine
members.what: Hardware-vectored handler code that preempts normal execution to service an event, doing minimal work at interrupt context before returning.

members.name: Interrupt Vector Table
members.what: A table of handler entry addresses, indexed by exception/interrupt number, through which the CPU dispatches to the right ISR; firmware populates and sometimes relocates it (e.g. VTOR).

members.name: Interval Arithmetic
members.what: Representing each numeric quantity as an interval [lo, hi] guaranteed to contain the true value, with arithmetic rules (and outward/directed rounding) that propagate the bounds through every operation.

members.name: iohw.h Standard Hardware I/O Interface
members.what: A standardized C/C++ macro interface (iord/iowr on abstract register designators) that isolates device-register access from platform addressing details.

members.name: Kahan Summation
members.what: Accumulates a floating-point sum together with a running compensation term that captures the low-order bits lost by each addition, keeping total rounding error near machine epsilon instead of growing with n.

members.name: Memory-Mapped Register Access
members.what: Address peripheral hardware registers as (volatile-qualified) memory locations through typed pointers or structure overlays, with disciplined read/write ordering.

members.name: Method Object
aka: Replace Method with Method Object (Fowler, Refactoring)
Replace Function with Command (Fowler, Refactoring 2nd ed.)
members.what: Reify a complex method as its own class: parameters and local variables become instance variables, the body becomes small methods on the new object.

members.name: Money
members.what: A value object representing a monetary amount together with its currency, with allocation/rounding rules that conserve the total.

members.name: Object Mother
members.what: A factory class dedicated to producing ready-made, semantically meaningful example objects (a standard customer, an overdue invoice) for use across many tests.

members.name: Organizing Files in Modular C Programs
members.what: Named patterns for splitting a C codebase into header/implementation files and directories so modules stay self-contained with explicit interfaces.

members.name: Page Object
members.what: A test-side object that wraps a UI page or fragment behind an application-specific API, so tests manipulate intention-revealing methods instead of raw HTML/widget structure.

members.name: Parameterized Test
members.what: A single test-logic body executed once per row of a table of inputs and expected outputs, with each row reported as its own test case.

members.name: PID Controller
members.what: A periodic feedback loop computing an actuator command as the weighted sum of proportional, integral, and derivative terms of the setpoint error, implemented as a fixed-rate update with output clamping, integrator anti-windup, and derivativ

members.name: Polling
members.what: The software repeatedly samples device or data status - periodically on a timer or opportunistically in the main loop - instead of being interrupted.

members.name: Property-Based Testing
members.what: Tests state universally quantified properties of the code; a harness draws random inputs from composable generators, checks the property, and shrinks any failing input to a minimal counterexample.

members.name: Pseudorandom Number Generator
members.what: A deterministic state machine that expands a seed into a stream of statistically random-looking numbers, giving reproducible randomness on demand.

members.name: Saturation Arithmetic
members.what: Arithmetic in which results exceeding the representable range clamp to the minimum/maximum value instead of wrapping around.

members.name: Serial Number Arithmetic
members.what: Compare fixed-width, wrapping sequence numbers using modular half-range rules so ordering remains correct across wraparound.

members.name: Service Stub
members.what: Removes dependence on a problematic external service during testing by substituting an in-process stand-in that implements the same gateway interface.

members.name: Shadow Register
members.what: Maintain a RAM copy of a hardware register's intended contents, perform all read-modify-write logic on the copy, and write the whole copy to the device.

members.name: Software-Module with Global State
members.what: Implement a module whose related functions operate on shared file-scope (static global) state inside the module, with initialization/cleanup functions for that state, while callers hold no instance at all.

members.name: Stateless Software-Module
members.what: Provide a set of logically related functions that keep no state between calls: every resource a function needs is acquired and released inside the call, so the caller owns nothing and calls are independent.

members.name: Super Loop
members.what: Structure the whole application as one endless main loop that calls each task function in turn, with ISRs as the only asynchronous activity.

members.name: Test Data Builder
members.what: A builder with sensible defaults and fluent with-methods used in tests to construct complex objects, overriding only the fields relevant to each test.

members.name: Test Double
members.what: A substitute object installed in place of a production dependency during a test; the family spans dummy, fake, stub, spy, and mock by increasing behavioral sophistication.

members.name: Test Fixture
members.what: The arranged pre-test state (objects, data, environment) a test depends on, built fresh per test or shared across tests under an explicit strategy.

members.name: Typesafe Register Access via C++ Templates
members.what: Hardware registers and bitfields modeled as template types so illegal accesses fail at compile time while generated code equals hand-written volatile pokes.

members.name: X-Macro
members.what: A single macro list of entries is expanded multiple times with different definitions of X to generate parallel artifacts (enums, string tables, dispatch tables) from one source of truth.
